provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Count and write 1 to 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count objects up to 10.
The pupils should be able to write numbers from 1 to 10.

Introduction:
We have learned numbers before. Today we will count and write numbers.

Content:
Count your fingers. One, two, three, four, five. Count your toes. Six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Write each number on the board. Use your finger to write in the air.

Class activity:
Give each pupil 10 beans. Count them together. Write the number on paper.

Evaluation questions:
Count how many books are on the table.
Write the number 5 on your slate.
Which number comes after 3?

Summary:
We can count and write numbers from 1 to 10.

topics.title: Count 11 to 20
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count objects from 11 to 20.
The pupils should be able to write numbers from 11 to 20.

Introduction:
We know numbers up to 10. Now we will learn numbers up to 20.

Content:
Use bundles of ten sticks. One bundle and one stick is 11. One bundle and two sticks is 12. Continue to 20. Write the numbers on the board.

Class activity:
Make groups of ten pupils. Add one pupil at a time and count to 20.

Evaluation questions:
Count how many chairs are in the class.
Write the number 15 on your slate.
What comes after 17?

Summary:
We can count and write numbers from 11 to 20.

topics.title: Count 21 to 30
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers from 21 to 30.
The pupils should be able to write numbers from 21 to 30.

Introduction:
We learned numbers up to 20. Now we will jump to 30.

Content:
Use a number line on the floor. Pupils jump from 21 to 30. Say each number as you jump. Write the numbers on the board.

Class activity:
Stand in a line. Each pupil says the next number from 21 to 30.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 21 to 30.
Write the number 25 on your slate.
What comes before 28?

Summary:
We can count and write numbers from 21 to 30.

topics.title: Count 31 to 50
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers from 31 to 50.
The pupils should be able to fill in missing numbers in a sequence.

Introduction:
We know numbers up to 30. Today we will learn up to 50.

Content:
Write numbers from 31 to 50 on the board. Leave some numbers blank. Pupils fill in the missing numbers. Count together.

Class activity:
Write numbers on cards. Mix them up. Pupils put them in order from 31 to 50.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 31 to 50.
Fill in the blank: 32, __, 34.
Write the number 40 on your slate.

Summary:
We can count numbers from 31 to 50.

topics.title: Counting 1 to 50 fast
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers from 1 to 50 quickly.
The pupils should be able to identify missing numbers in a sequence.

Introduction:
We have learned numbers up to 50. Now we will count fast.

Content:
Count in turns around the circle. Each pupil says one number. Fill gaps on the board when numbers are missing.

Class activity:
Play a counting game. Pass a ball and count from 1 to 50.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 50 without stopping.
What number is missing: 10, 11, __, 13?
Count backwards from 50 to 1.

Summary:
We can count fast from 1 to 50.

topics.title: More and fewer
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify which group has more objects.
The pupils should be able to identify which group has fewer objects.

Introduction:
Sometimes we have more things. Sometimes we have fewer things. Let us learn about more and fewer.

Content:
Show two groups of objects. One group has more objects. The other has fewer. Circle the group with more. Circle the group with fewer.

Class activity:
Give pupils two groups of beans. Count each group. Which has more? Which has fewer?

Evaluation questions:
Which group has more books?
Circle the group with fewer pencils.
If I have 5 sweets and you have 3, who has more?

Summary:
We can tell which group has more and which has fewer.

topics.title: Simple addition with objects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add two small groups of objects.
The pupils should be able to write the answer to simple addition.

Introduction:
Sometimes we put things together. This is called addition.

Content:
Show two sweets. Add three more sweets. Count all sweets together. This is 2 + 3 = 5. Use objects to show more examples.

Class activity:
Give pupils counters. Add two groups and count the total.

Evaluation questions:
2 + 3 = ?
If I have 4 pencils and you give me 2, how many do I have?
Count and add: 1 + 4 = ?

Summary:
We can add two small groups of objects.

topics.title: Simple subtraction with objects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to subtract objects from a group.
The pupils should be able to count what is left after subtraction.

Introduction:
Sometimes we take things away. This is called subtraction.

Content:
Show five balls. Take away two balls. Count how many are left. This is 5-2 = 3. Use objects to show more examples.

Class activity:
Give pupils 10 beans. Ask them to take away 3 and count what is left.

Evaluation questions:
5-2 = ?
If I have 7 sweets and eat 3, how many are left?
Count and subtract: 9-4 = ?

Summary:
We can subtract and count what is left.

topics.title: Shapes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify circle, triangle, and square.
The pupils should be able to find shapes in the classroom.

Introduction:
We see shapes all around us. Let us learn about some shapes.

Content:
Show a circle. It is round. Show a triangle. It has three sides. Show a square. It has four equal sides. Find these shapes in the room.

Class activity:
Go on a shape hunt. Find circles, triangles, and squares in the classroom.

Evaluation questions:
What shape is a clock?
How many sides does a triangle have?
Point to something square in the room.

Summary:
We can identify and find shapes around us.

topics.title: Revision and number games
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers from 1 to 50.
The pupils should be able to identify shapes.

Introduction:
We have learned many things this term. Let us revise with games.

Content:
Play number bingo with numbers up to 50. Play shape hunt in the playground. Count objects and identify shapes.

Class activity:
Play number bingo. Call out numbers and pupils cover them on their cards.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 50.
What shape has three sides?
Play a counting game with a friend.

Summary:
We can count and identify shapes through games.
